failure: The first backup implementation called fsync on a read-only Windows file handle, which returned Errno 9 and prevented backup completion.
repair: Open the completed temporary SQLite copy with a writable binary handle for the durability flush, then rerun the unchanged recovery and CLI cases.
second_observed_failure: After the fsync repair, five cases passed but corrupt/truncated verification could retain a Windows file lock long enough to break fixture cleanup because ordinary verification opened the source read-write.
second_repair: Add an explicit read-only SQLite verification connection and use it for backup/restore source and copied-file checks; the unchanged six-case recovery suite then passed.
nonclaim: Windows local fixture failure only; it does not establish behavior on other filesystems or crash conditions.
